proof_summary: Couple the mass-(n+1\) evolution to the mass-(n\) evolution as the latter plus one marked particle, which stays put or moves one cell right according to the parity of its current cell; conservation, contiguity of support, and the evolution of the leading block of ones show that when the mass-(n\) system stabilizes, this particle is in position (n-1\) or (n-2\). From these positions it takes respectively one or two further updates to extend the stable block of ones, while the coupling and minimality of stabilization exclude any earlier stabilization.
